result.markdown: --- title: "[split_episodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Convert repeated-measurement data into counting-process (episode-split) format. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_tvc.py#L19-L285){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python split_episodes( baseline, visits, *, id, time, event, visit_time, covariates=None, baseline_covariates=None, carry_forward=True, format=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Takes a subject-level baseline table and a long-format visits table, and merges them into the interval-per-row counting-process layout required by `Surv.counting()` and `CoxPH`. Each row in the output represents a constant-covariate interval `(tstart, tstop]` for one subject. The covariate value measured at visit time `v` applies to the interval `[v, next_v)`. The event indicator is 1 only on the final interval for subjects who experienced the event; all earlier intervals carry 0. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [baseline]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The subject-level table. Must contain the `id`, `time`, and `event` columns. It may have one row per subject, or it may be the same long table as `visits` when that table repeats the follow-up time and event on every row. In that case the first row of each subject is used, after checking that `time`, `event`, and any `baseline_covariates` are constant within the subject. [visits]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per (subject, visit). Must contain the `id` and `visit_time` columns. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column name linking `baseline` and `visits`. [time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column in `baseline` giving the end of follow-up (right-censored exit time). [event]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column in `baseline` giving the event indicator. [visit_time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column in `visits` giving the measurement time for each row. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The columns of `visits` to carry as time-varying covariates. The default (`None`) uses every column other than `id` and `visit_time`. [baseline_covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The columns of `baseline` to carry as time-fixed covariates. The default (`None`) uses every column other than `id`, `time`, and `event` when `baseline` has one row per subject, and none when it repeats subjects (a long table usually holds per-visit columns that are not fixed in time). [carry_forward]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), the last observed covariate value is carried forward to the end of follow-up (LOCF), producing a final interval `(last_visit, time]`. If `False`, follow-up is truncated at the last visit; the trailing interval is dropped and the subject is effectively administratively censored there. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. - `None` (default): auto-detect, trying Polars first, then Pandas, then PyArrow. - `"pandas"`: return a `pandas.DataFrame`. - `"polars"`: return a `polars.DataFrame`. - `"pyarrow"`: return a `pyarrow.Table`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Counting-process dataset with columns `(id, tstart, tstop, event, [time-fixed covariates], [time-varying covariates])`. Ready to pass directly to `Surv.counting(tstart, tstop, event)` and `CoxPH.fit()`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If required columns are missing, if any visit time exceeds the subject's follow-up end, or if the resulting dataset is empty. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Build a minimal TVC dataset and fit a Cox model: ::: {#bf2cf4fd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import greenwood as gw baseline = pd.DataFrame({ "id": [1, 2, 3], "time": [10.0, 8.0, 12.0], "event": [1, 0, 1], }) visits = pd.DataFrame({ "id": [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3], "day": [0.0, 5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0, 8.0], "bili": [1.2, 2.4, 0.8, 3.1, 2.9, 4.0], }) long = gw.split_episodes( baseline=baseline, visits=visits, id="id", time="time", event="event", visit_time="day" ) y = gw.Surv.counting(start=long["tstart"], stop=long["tstop"], event=long["event"]) cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(y, covariates=["bili"], data=long) ``` :::
